title: Integrated Finance Playbook: Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement & Revenue Recognition (2027)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook documents Redwood Inference's integrated finance operating procedures for annual budgeting and rolling forecasting, contract lifecycle and legal review, procurement approvals and execution, and revenue recognition / billing practices. It is intended as the single source of truth for finance, legal, procurement, and business owners to ensure consistency, compliance, and audit readiness.

Scope:
Applies to all Redwood business units and legal entities globally; covers:
- Annual operating and capital budgets, quarterly re-forecasts, and rolling 12-months cash forecasts
- Contract intake, negotiation, signature, and archival workflows for customer, vendor, and partner agreements
- Procurement request, sourcing, approval and PO issuance for goods and services
- Revenue recognition, invoicing cadence, and billing dispute resolution processes

Key principles:
- Separation of duties: approvals, accounting entries, and custody of assets are separated where feasible.
- Threshold-based controls: approval levels scale with financial impact.
- Auditability: every material contract, PO, and revenue event must have an auditable trail (owner, approver, date, attachments).
- Timeliness: budget cadence and billing schedules are predictable; exceptions are escalated.

Roles and responsibilities

- Finance (FP&A): owns budgeting and forecasting cadence, budget templates, variance reporting, and financial consolidation.
- Legal: owns contract templates, risk review, redlines, and signature authority guardrails.
- Procurement: owns vendor onboarding, master vendor list, PO issuance, and supplier performance tracking.
- Business Owner / Cost Center Manager: proposes budget lines, approves spend requests, and verifies vendor receipts.
- Revenue Operations (RevOps) / Billing: owns invoicing, subscription metering, billing reconciliations, and revenue close activities.

Budgeting and forecasting process

Overview:
Annual budget is prepared on a fiscal-year basis (FY) with a detailed monthly granularity for the first 12 months and quarterly for the outer 12-14 months. A rolling 12-month forecast is updated monthly.

Cadence and timeline (example FY2027):
1. July-August: Strategic planning input from product, engineering and GTM; preliminary revenue targets set.
2. September: Budget templates issued to owners; top-down headcount and capital guidance provided.
3. October: Cost center owners submit detailed budgets and hiring plans.
4. November: FP&A consolidates, runs scenario analysis, produces executive package.
5. December: Executive review and approval; budgets loaded into ERP.
6. Monthly: Rolling 12-month forecast updated by 7th business day; variance commentary required for >5% movement.

Required artifacts:
- Budget template (CSV/Google Sheet) with GL mapping
- Headcount plan (per role, start date, comp assumptions)
- CapEx request form (justification, depreciation life, owner)

Approval matrix (examples):
- Up to $10k: Cost center manager approval.
- $10k-$100k: Department head + Finance approver.
- $100k-$500k: VP Finance + Legal (if contractual).
- >$500k: CFO + CEO approval and Board notification for capital commitments.

Procurement procedures

Request and sourcing:
1. Initiation: Business owner submits an electronic Purchase Request (PR) in procurement tool including SOW, budget code, and estimated value.
2. Sourcing: Procurement evaluates suppliers; required competitive bids:
   - < $25k: one quote acceptable for approved vendors.
   - $25k-$250k: minimum two written quotes.
   - > $250k: formal RFP and procurement committee review.

Vendor onboarding checklist:
- Completed W-9 (or local tax equivalent) and payment remit details.
- Valid insurance certificates (if required by contract).
- Security & privacy questionnaire (for vendors with data access).
- Tax and sanctions screening completed.

Approval and PO issuance:
- Procurement issues PO only after budget confirmation and contract (if applicable) signed.
- POs are generated from approved PRs and must reference budget line and cost center.
- Goods/services should not be ordered without PO unless emergency approval documented and later regularized.

Receiving and invoice processing:
- Business owner confirms receipt of goods/services in procurement tool.
- Vendor invoice must match PO and receiving record; discrepancies routed to the business owner for resolution.
- AP processes payment per vendor terms (standard Net 30 unless otherwise negotiated).

Contracts and legal process

Intake and triage:
1. All agreements submitted via Contracts intake form (link in Related Pages).
2. Triage: Legal classifies into Standard Customer SLA, Standard Vendor, NDAs, MSA, Data Processing Agreement (DPA), or High-risk (requires senior counsel).

Standard templates and playbooks:
- Use approved template (Customer MSA v3.2, Vendor Agreement v2.1, DPA v1.4) located in the Contracts library.
- Standard redlines are predefined; deviations require documented business justification.

Review & approvals:
1. Legal review for risk profile and required clauses (IP, confidentiality, liability caps, indemnities, export control, data residency).
2. Finance reviews for payment terms, revenue implications, and recognition triggers.
3. Security/Privacy review for data processing and access.
4. Signature: signature authority defined in Signature Authority Matrix; electronic signatures accepted where supported.

Contract repository and retention:
- All fully executed contracts must be uploaded to the centralized contract repository (document store) within 3 business days.
- Retention policy: retain executed contracts for the life of the agreement + 7 years (or longer when required by law).

Revenue recognition & billing policy

Revenue recognition principles:
- Redwood follows ASC 606 / IFRS 15 principles: identify contract(s) with customer, identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price to performance obligations, recognize revenue when (or as) performance obligations are satisfied.
- For subscription services: revenue recognized ratably over the service period, unless distinct performance obligations indicate otherwise.
- For usage-based billing (hosted API tokens, embeddings): revenue recognized as usage occurs; meter data must be stored and reconciled.

Billing cadence and invoicing:
- Default billing cadence: monthly in arrears for usage; monthly or annual for subscription plans as per contract.
- Invoice content must include: contract/PO reference, billing period, quantity/units, unit price, subtotal, taxes, payment terms.
- Billing disputes: customer must notify within 30 days; RevOps and Finance coordinate resolution. Disputed amounts are documented and, where appropriate, placed in dispute hold while undisputed amounts are invoiced and collected.

Revenue close activities (monthly close checklist):
- Reconcile invoiced amounts to ledger and meter reports.
- Accrue unbilled revenue for delivered services not yet invoiced.
- Verify deferred revenue balance and amortization schedules for subscriptions and prepayments.
- Document manual journal entries with supporting rationale and approver.

Audit controls and evidence

Minimum artifacts to retain per material transaction:
- Approved PR and PO, vendor/vendor onboarding records.
- Fully executed contract and all redlines/versions.
- Invoice, receiving confirmation, and payment evidence.
- Billing meter files and reconciliation reports for usage-based revenue.
- Budget submission and approval trail for material variances.

Operational KPIs and thresholds (sample):
- Forecast accuracy: target mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) <6% for total revenue on a rolling 12-month basis.
- Days Sales Outstanding (DSO): target <45 days.
- PO-to-invoice match rate: target >95%.
- Contract repository completeness: 100% of executed contracts uploaded within 3 business days.

Exceptions and escalations

- Exceptions to standard procurement or contracting processes (e.g., emergency purchases, non-standard indemnities) must be documented and escalated to Finance Manager and Senior Counsel.
- Any revenue recognition judgment items (e.g., significant variable consideration, rebates, complex bundling) must be escalated to Head of Accounting for review and documented with supporting analysis.

Appendices

A. Signature Authority Matrix (summary):
- Cost center manager: approvals up to $10k
- Director: up to $100k
- VP: up to $500k
- CFO: up to $2M
- CEO: > $2M (or as required by Board resolution)

B. Common GL mappings (examples):
| Category | GL Account |
| Operations - Cloud | 5000 |
| R&D - Contractor | 6005 |
| Sales & Marketing - Events | 5200 |
